Repetitive, looping thoughts can be exhausting, and it's frustrating when you can't seem to shut them off. A few things can help interrupt the cycle: try grounding yourself in the present moment by focusing on your senses—naming what you see, hear, and feel around you. Sometimes writing the thought down gets it "out of your head" and onto paper, which can loosen its grip. Physical movement, like a short walk, can also help shift your mental state.

It can also help to set aside a specific "worry time"—a few minutes to let the thought have your attention—so it feels less like it's demanding attention all day. If these thoughts are causing significant distress, disrupting your sleep, or feel impossible to control, it may be worth talking with a counselor or doctor, as this can sometimes point to something like anxiety or OCD that responds well to support.

You don't have to just endure this alone—reaching out is a strong step.
